<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

For every word-by-word reading: where grouping recovers the words, reading every encoded sequence gives the meanings of its words exactly when each word is read as its meaning. For acquired lexicons: wherever the transition record groups the two-word encoding (six local bond conditions), interpreting every encoded sequence equals the assembly of its atoms exactly when each word form resolves to its atom. The specified history, which forms grouping and acquires form-to-known-operation bindings from four individually ambiguous encounters, is an instance. A separate finite-support witness executes the result.

Canonical source: [AcquiredBinding.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/inquiry-root/AcquiredBinding.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- Existing operations, elementary categories, grouping algorithm, three-operation repertoire, intersection update and encounter schedule are supplied; the successful history has sufficient support.
- General correctness requires the target in the repertoire and in each relevant admitted encounter; source-exclusion judgments for correction are separately supplied.

What is acquired is a new form-to-available-operation relationship; scene lists represent accessible alternatives and require independent perceptual/social correspondence.

<a id="检验与边界-validation-and-boundaries"></a>
## Validation and boundaries

Fresh Lean 4.29.1 build: 23 new theorems / 41 declaration audits, with 247 inherited audits separately rebuilt. Author counterreview and primary-evidence comparison; no independent acceptance or new experiment.

Does not derive the full meanings of prior operations, category/attention origins or source-judgment reliability; not a proof of complete semantics, infant neural mechanisms or evolutionary psychology.

- Omitting the target can create a wrong unique binding; repeated ambiguity does not identify a meaning; excluding sound evidence preserves error, and finite support can prevent execution.
